name: Sir John Beckwith
current_role: Founder and chairman, Pacific Investments (London private investment group: real estate, asset management, private equity)
profile: Sir John Beckwith (b. 1947) trained as a chartered accountant, then in 1971 co-founded property company London & Edinburgh Trust with his brother Peter, building it into one of the UK's top ten real estate firms. He later founded Rutland Trust (1986) and Pacific Investments (1993), which he runs with his partners. Knighted in 2002 for services to youth sport.
interesting_fact: He is the founder and president of the Youth Sport Trust, the UK charity using sport to change young people's lives. He was knighted for services to youth sport in 2002.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding London & Edinburgh Trust at 24, he qualified as a chartered accountant at Beresford Lye & Co and worked at Arthur Andersen (1969-71). A self-described sport fanatic, he had run four marathons by 2011. Loughborough University gave him an honorary DLitt in 2000.

name: Dan Houser
current_role: Founder, Absurd Ventures (games, books, comics, audio fiction and animation studio)
profile: London-born co-founder, with brother Sam, of Rockstar Games (1998). As head writer he shaped Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption and Bully. He left Rockstar in March 2020 and announced Absurd Ventures in 2023. It has since released the audio series and novel A Better Paradise (2025), the Dark Horse comic American Caper, and the 'Absurdaverse' animated universe.
interesting_fact: He started in 1995 as a part-time CD-ROM tester at BMG Interactive. He and Sam signed DMA Design's 'Race'n'Chase' to BMG and renamed it Grand Theft Auto, then founded Rockstar in New York after Take-Two bought BMG Interactive.
deep_cut_fact: He read geography at Christ Church, Oxford (matriculated 1993). He has voice credits in GTA: Liberty City Stories and Vice City Stories. He sits on the boards of the Rainforest Alliance and the Brooklyn Museum.
notes: Historically press-shy, but now actively promoting A Better Paradise and Absurd projects, so a podcast pitch tied to the book or studio launch is plausible. Best route: press@absurdventures.com. The studio's contact page jokes 'We probably won't reply.'
